value.name: Lucia argues for preserving the house
value.description: Lucia insists the house is her mother's sanctuary and should remain a place of love and connection rather than be sold.
evidence: she poured her heart into this home; it was a sanctuary for all of us. I believe she wanted it to remain a place of love and connection, not just another asset to sell.

value.name: Daniel demands the house be sold
value.description: Daniel rejects sentimental arguments and says the house must be sold so the family can move on and pay their bills.
evidence: Daniel: "That's all well and good, Lucia, but love and connection won't pay the bills—this house needs to be sold so we can move on with our lives."

value.name: Rosa urges protecting their mother's legacy
value.description: Rosa acknowledges Daniel's practical concerns but argues the house represents their mother's legacy and should be protected.
evidence: Rosa: "Daniel, I see your point, but think about what our mother truly wanted; this house was her legacy, a testament to the love she nurtured here—it's worth protecting."

value.name: Asha calls for balancing memory and practicality
value.description: Asha says the family should honor the house's emotional legacy while also making practical decisions, suggesting Miguel's presence can help them remember that balance.
evidence: Asha: I understand the urgency to act, Daniel, but we must also honor the emotional legacy tied to this house; perhaps Miguel’s presence can help us remember that there is value in both the memories and practical decisions we face.

value.name: Miguel reminds family of mother's dream
value.description: Miguel invokes their mother's dream of a loving home and asks them to remember it while deciding what to do.
evidence: Miguel: Your mother dreamed of a home filled with love. Let’s remember that as we discuss what to do.

value.name: Lucia intensifies defense of the house
value.description: Lucia argues the house is a living testament to their mother's love and should not be treated as a disposable financial burden.
evidence: Lucia: "Exactly, Miguel! This house isn't just bricks and mortar; it's a living testament to our mother's love. She envisioned it as a refuge for those who truly cherished it, not as a financial burden to be discarded."

value.name: Daniel warns nostalgia will cause ruin
value.description: Daniel counters that sentimentality is dangerous and warns the family that failing to sell quickly could lead to financial ruin.
evidence: Daniel: "Living testament or not, Lucia, we can't let nostalgia blind us to reality; if we don't act fast, this 'refuge' will become our financial ruin."

value.name: Lucia rejects quick sale
value.description: Lucia insists the issue is honoring their mother's memory and legacy, not simply selling the house to the highest bidder.
evidence: Lucia: "Daniel, it's not just about money—it's about honoring Mom's memory and the legacy she left behind; she wanted this house to be a home for those who truly valued it, not just a quick sale to the highest bidder."

value.name: Rosa supports Lucia's view
value.description: Rosa backs Lucia's argument by saying the house holds their mother's spirit and more of the family sentiment.
